threatening risks. manual checks by drivers or staff have proven insufficient to consistently prevent these dangerous oversights. news : times of india 2. problem statement there is an urgent need for a reliable, automated system to detect the presence of a child inside a school bus — especially after completion of a trip — and trigger timely alerts to relevant stakeholders before harm can occur. current practices rely heavily on manual inspection, which can fail due to human error, fatigue, or distraction. a technological solution must ensure that no child remains unnoticed inside a vehicle after the bus completes its route, irrespective of whether bus staff remember to check. 3. core requirements & considerations ( merged ) the proposed solution must address the following : ● automated presence detection : the system should accurately detect human presence in the bus interior even when occupants are still or inactive ( e. g., asleep ). ● environmental reliability : it must function under varying conditions ( heat inside parked bus, lighting changes, vibration, noise ). ● low false alerts : minimize incorrect alarms through robust sensing and intelligent processing. ● immediate alerts : trigger multi - channel notifications ( audible alarm in bus, sms / app / in - system alerts to transport authorities, school administration, and caregivers ). ● independent operation : work reliably even without continuous internet — with fallback storage of logs and delayed uploads. ● retrofit friendly & cost - effective : compatible with existing fleets without major modifications ; easy to maintain and scalable for large bus fleets. the system should be capable of detecting the presence of a child before or after the bus is parked, shut down, or switched off and must support escalation workflows if initial alerts go unacknowledged. 4. deliverables ( submission requirements ) all solution proposals should be submitted in powerpoint ( ppt ) format and must include the following key components : a. proposed system & architecture ● block diagram of the solution ● detection approach ( e. g., sensor suite, algorithms ) ● data flow and alert mechanism b. detection methodology ● sensors and technologies used ● how detection accuracy is achieved ● strategies to reduce false positives / negatives c. bill of materials ( bom ) ● complete list of hardware parts ● estimated cost per unit ● vendor suggestions / part alternatives d. alerting & notification strategy ● alarm triggers ( in - bus, external notifications ) ● stakeholder escalation plan ● communication methods ( sms, mobile apps, dashboards ) e. deployment plan ● installation process ● testing and validation approach ● maintenance and calibration recommendations f. safety & operational considerations ● power backup strategy ● environmental tolerance ( heat, dust, vibration ) ● privacy considerations ( if cameras used ) 5. expected outcome the proposed solution must demonstrate how it will ensure no child remains undetected in school buses, increasing safety and reducing the risk of similar
